Status: proposal, not implemented (FEATURE_BACKLOG.md #105). Decisions still open are listed at the
end. Once implemented, the current state moves into `docs/log-formats.md`
and this file into `docs/archive/`.

## Goal

Log formats can be shipped as files beside `philogg.html` (or the desktop
executable) and are picked up automatically at start, without being baked
into the HTML and without an import step:

- the homepage serves the tour's welcome format next to the hosted app;
- an admin or installer drops company formats into a folder and every
  user on that machine has them;
- `philogg.html` itself ships with only the builtin Default and Plain text
  formats.

## Today

- Formats and filename rules live in the session-cache IndexedDB
  (`logFormats`, `formatRules` stores), per browser origin or webview
  profile. They are not part of the desktop `settings.json` mirror, which
  only covers `philogg-*` `localStorage` keys.
- Baked into `philogg.html`: `fmt-default` (builtin), `fmt-plaintext`
  (code level) and three demo seeds (`DEMO_SEED_FORMATS`: App log,
  Syslog RFC 5424, their meta format). `loadFormatConfig` re-seeds a demo
  format on every boot when it is missing, so a deleted demo format comes
  back after a reload.
- The welcome format is not baked in: the tour session file carries it in
  a file record's `logFormat` field, and `ensureSessionLogFormat` saves it
  into the visitor's own formats.
- A `.logformat.json` file (`philogg-log-format` v1, with
  `fileNamePatterns`) can be imported through Open → Import…. Meta formats
  cannot be exported to that file today (`normalizeLogFormatExport`
  accepts regex, pattern and json modes only).

## Proposal: provided formats

A **provided format** is read from a file at every start and kept in
memory only. It is a read-only layer next to the user's own formats:

| | Own format | Provided format |
|---|---|---|
| Stored in | IndexedDB | the file; never written to IndexedDB |
| Edit / delete | yes | no; **Duplicate** creates an editable own copy |
| Id | random `fmt-…` | `fmt-provided-<slug of the file name>`, stable across starts so session-cache pins survive |
| Filename rules | own rules | the file's `fileNamePatterns`, read-only, ranked after the user's own rules |
| Update | edit in the dialog | replace the file; the next start uses it |
| Removed | delete | file gone → the format is gone; a pinned file behaves like one pinned to a deleted format |

The Format Manager lists provided formats with a "Provided" tag and the
source location as tooltip. `ensureSessionLogFormat` also matches provided
formats, so a session that embeds an identical format reuses the provided
one instead of copying it into the user's store.

**File format**: the existing `.logformat.json` unchanged, one format per
file. A meta format needs one extension: its targets referenced by name
(`targetFormatNames`), resolved against provided and own formats at load.

## Where the files are found

| Runtime | Location | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| Desktop (installer) | `<install-dir>/formats/*.logformat.json` (machine-wide) and `<config-dir>/PhiLogg/formats/` (per user) | Rust reads both folders at window creation and bakes the list into the init script, like the `settings.json` hydration (`inject.rs`): available before the page script runs, no IPC race |
| Desktop (portable) | `<exe-dir>/formats/` | same, via `settings::portable_dir()` |
| Hosted (http/https, homepage) | `formats/index.json` next to the page, listing the file names | one `fetch` at boot; a 404 means no provided formats, silently |
| `file://` (HTML on a share) | `philogg-formats.js` next to the HTML | `fetch` is blocked on `file://`, a classic `<script src>` is not; the file calls `PhiLoggFormats.push(...)` with the format objects and is generated from `.logformat.json` files by a small script (`scripts/format-bundle.js`) |

The desktop build does not watch the folders; a restart picks up changes.
A file that fails `normalizeLogFormatExport` is skipped with a one-line
notice in Settings → Log Formats (name and reason), never a boot error.

## What changes elsewhere

- **Demo seeds leave the HTML**: the three `DEMO_SEED_FORMATS` become files
  in `examples/formats/` (and, if wanted, on the homepage). This also ends
  the re-seed-after-delete behaviour.
- **Homepage**: `scripts/build-site.js` writes `app/formats/index.json` and
  `app/formats/welcome.logformat.json`. The tour session can keep its
  `logFormat` field (it stays usable as a downloaded file); with the
  provided format present it is reused, not duplicated.
- **Rollout**: an installer step, a software-distribution package or a copy
  script places `*.logformat.json` into `formats/` next to the executable
  (or into the user's config folder). The Windows installer can ship a
  default `formats/` folder of its own.
- **Tests**: a jsdom group for the hosted route (mocked `fetch`), the
  injected desktop list, the `file://` script route, read-only UI,
  Duplicate, stable ids and rule ranking; `cargo test` for the folder
  reader (missing folder, invalid JSON, non-format files ignored).

## Phasing

1. Provided-format layer in `philogg.html` (read-only list, Duplicate,
   rules, `ensureSessionLogFormat`) plus the hosted route; homepage ships
   the welcome format; demo seeds move to `examples/formats/`.
2. Desktop folders (Rust reader + init-script injection).
3. `file://` script bundle and meta formats by target name.

## Open decisions

1. Which runtimes matter first: desktop + hosted (proposed), or also
   `file://` from the start?
2. Read-only layer (proposed) or a one-time import into the user's own
   formats on first sight (simpler, but later file updates would not
   arrive)?
3. Remove the three demo formats from the HTML (proposed)?
